title_en: Land Traffic Act B.E. 2522 (1979), consolidated text
issuing_authority: Office of the Council of State
governs: Section 139(6) empowers the Head of Traffic Officers to set vehicle speeds within the rates fixed by ministerial regulation
notes: Section 139 at pp. 34-35. Section 139 has 21 sub-paragraphs; speed is only (6).
Checked because section 139 might have been amended. It was not: a full-text search for the numeral 139 returns 19 hits, all in the running head.

title_en: Ministerial Regulation Prescribing Vehicle Speeds on Designated National or Rural Highways B.E. 2564 (2021)
governs: 120 km/h on designated stretches, subject to three physical conditions; full table by vehicle class, including 65 km/h for three-wheelers
notes: No commencement clause found in the text, so no in-force date is asserted. A fourth condition applies: the Director of National Highways must gazette each stretch separately.

title_en: Ministerial Regulation Prescribing Speeds for Driving on Roadways B.E. 2564 (2021)
enabling_provision: Land Traffic Act B.E. 2522, s.5 para.1 and s.67 para.1
governs: General speed table by area and vehicle class: 80 km/h in built-up areas, 90 outside, 100 with a central divider; three-wheelers 45/55/65
notes: In force 240 days after publication; the in-force date here is that calculation, not a date printed in the instrument. Clause 10 gives priority to regulations issued under the Highway Act, which is the link to TH-03. Clause 3 leaves the definition of a community area to the Head of Traffic Officers with no quantitative threshold. Repeals the 1979 and 1981 regulations.

title_en: Notification of the Director of National Highways on Designated Routes for Vehicle Speeds (No. 1)
governs: Designates specific kilometre ranges where 120 km/h applies: Highway 32, 45.9 km

title_en: Notification of the Director of National Highways on Designated Routes for Vehicle Speeds (No. 2)
Notification of the Director of National Highways on Designated Routes for Vehicle Speeds (No. 3)
notes: Highway 9 is Kanchanaphisek. The designated stretch is Bang Khae to Khlong Maha Sawat, 8.2 km, against 180.2 km recorded at 120 km/h in the challenge dataset.

title_en: Notification of the Director of National Highways on Designated Routes for Vehicle Speeds (No. 4)
notes: Whether a No. 5 exists has not been established. The four notices together cover roughly 250 km.

title_en: Regulation of the Head of Traffic Officers in the Bangkok Metropolis on Speed Limits and Prohibition of Horn Use B.E. 2567 (2024)
issuing_authority: Head of Traffic Officers, Bangkok Metropolis (signed by the Deputy Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police acting for the Commissioner)
governs: 60 km/h on every road in the city; 50 km/h plus a horn ban on ten roads in the royal precinct; thirteen roads exempted from the 60
notes: Exemption 4.4 is Phahonyothin Road. The instrument states one reason for the change and none for any exemption; it sets no quantitative threshold, crash-rate trigger, study requirement or consultation step.

title_en: Regulation of Traffic Officers in the Bangkok Metropolis on Prescribing Vehicle Speeds B.E. 2561 (2018)
governs: 50 km/h on eight roads in the Dusit area
notes: Does not cover the thirteen roads exempted by TH-09, so the statutory limit on those roads is not established by either Bangkok instrument.

title_en: Regulation of Traffic Officers of Phatthalung Province on Prescribing Vehicle Speeds within the rates fixed by ministerial regulation B.E. 2561 (2018)
governs: Provincial speed limits by road and vehicle class
notes: Records that the limit was considered by the provincial land-traffic sub-committee under a Cabinet-approved measure, and lists the authority responsible for each road and its length. The two Bangkok instruments record none of these.

title_en: Regulation of Traffic Officers of Pattani Province on Prescribing Vehicle Speeds B.E. 2561 (2018)
governs: Provincial speed limits by road and vehicle class
notes: As TH-11: procedure, responsible authority and kilometre extents are all recorded.

governs: Section 112 'Limits of speed': the State Government or an authority it authorises may fix maxima, not exceeding those notified by the Central Government
notes: Section 112 at pp. 65-66. Section 112(2) names no office. Its proviso removes the notification requirement for measures lasting not more than one month.

title_en: S.O. 1522(E), maximum speeds by road class and vehicle category
issuing_authority: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
enabling_provision: Motor Vehicles Act 1988, proviso to s.112(1)
governs: Central ceiling by road class and vehicle category, including 50 km/h for three-wheeled vehicles on every road class
gazette: Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, s.3(ii), No. 1377
notes: File no. RT-11028/07/2017-MVL. Supersedes S.O. 1997(E) of 5 August 2014. Clause 2 sets a 5 per cent enforcement tolerance. The effect of this notification was the subject of later litigation and its current status has NOT been verified for this submission.

title_en: Government of Maharashtra, Motor Vehicles Department Manual, Part III, Control of Traffic
issuing_authority: Motor Vehicles Department, Government of Maharashtra
governs: Section 8.1 restates the speed-limit power under MVA s.112
notes: Section 8.1(3) names no office either, so the three-tier attribution used in earlier drafts is not supported by this document.

enabling_provision: Motor Vehicles Act 1988, s.115, and Government of Maharashtra notification MVA 0589/CR-1061/TRA-2 of 11 May 1990 as amended 27 September 1996
governs: 80 / 60 / 40 km/h on the Coastal Road for straight sections, tunnels and curves; bars several vehicle types including all three-wheelers
notes: Cited for who signs and under what delegated authority. The road opened in August 2025 and is NOT part of the network analysed here, whose Maharashtra extract dates from May 2025.

title_en: Government of Maharashtra notification MVA 0589/CR-1061/TRA-2, 11 May 1990, as amended 27 September 1996
governs: The instrument that would name which offices the State has authorised to fix speed limits
notes: Its number is known only because IN-04 cites it. Until it is obtained, the specific offices holding the power in Maharashtra are recorded as to be confirmed, not asserted. This is the single largest gap in the legal chain for India.

governs: Simulation of a 10 km/h limit reduction in Thailand under BIGRS; the source of the one-in-three figure for fatal and serious injuries
notes: Publicly hosted, so no copy is redistributed here. The one-in-three figure is from simulations, not measurement, and the source sentence begins 'Among a series of simulations and results'.

title_en: Pedestrian safety in developing countries: a systematic literature review and gap analysis
issuing_authority: Mubiru, J. and Evdorides, H., Future Transportation 6(1), 29
governs: Mean discrepancy of 30.9 per cent between predicted and observed countermeasure effectiveness across five LMIC case studies
notes: Report the mean with its standard deviation of 29.7 per cent and its 95 per cent confidence interval of -1.5 to 63.3 per cent, which crosses zero. The paper makes no statement that the ordering of interventions held.
